sources.massKg: TUNING KNOB (cruise/climb) — 11.5 t mid-mission weight (Citation Latitude MTOW ~13.97 t / 30,800 lb). Pinned by the FL430 cruise trim + sea-level climb tests.
sources.wingAreaM2: TUNING KNOB — 30.0 m^2, wing loading ~376 kg/m^2 at 11.5 t (mid-size-jet band). Citation Latitude published geometry pending source verification.
sources.wingSpanM: derived-consistent with aspectRatio: sqrt(AR*S) = sqrt(8.0*30.0) = 15.49 m.
sources.aspectRatio: TUNING KNOB — 8.0, typical mid-size-jet AR; b^2/S = 15.5^2/30.0 = 8.0.
sources.cl0: TUNING KNOB (cruise trim) — swept-wing zero-AoA lift; with clAlphaPerRad puts cruise AoA in a sane range at M0.78/FL430.
sources.clAlphaPerRad: TUNING KNOB (stall band) — 5.2/rad, a swept mid-jet-wing lift slope. Pinned by the sea-level clean-stall-speed band test (105-135 kt).
sources.stallAlphaRad: TUNING KNOB (stall band) — 17.2 deg (0.30 rad) clean critical AoA; CLmax_clean = 0.2 + 5.2*0.30 = 1.76. Pinned alongside clAlphaPerRad by the stall-speed band test.
sources.postStallDecayRad: TUNING KNOB — 0.18 rad fade width past the break, matching the b738/f5e pattern.
sources.cd0: TUNING KNOB (cruise Mach + SL climb + service ceiling) — 0.023, a realistic clean-jet parasite-drag coefficient (b738 uses 0.020). Honest now that biz sets its own turbofanCornerM (FL210) below FL430 cruise: holding cruise Mach then demands enough rated thrust that the same thrust, unlapsed at sea level, clears the >2500 fpm SL-climb target at this plausible cd0. Pinned together with maxPowerW and turbofanCornerM by the FL430-cruise + SL-climb + 45,000 ft-ceiling triple. Source verification pending for a published Citation figure.
sources.gearDragCd0: TUNING KNOB — 0.02, in the spec's ~0.015-0.02 mid-jet gear/doors range (top of range for a smaller, less-faired gear bay than the 737).
sources.speedbrakeCd0: TUNING KNOB (#51) — 0.045, the Citation-class airbrake/spoiler parasitic-drag increment (~2.25x clean cd0), scaled down from the b738's 0.05 for the smaller airframe. Source verification pending.
sources.oswaldE: TUNING KNOB — 0.80, typical transport/bizjet span efficiency.
sources.cyBeta: TUNING KNOB — -0.85/rad bizjet side-force slope, slightly less than the 737's -0.9 (smaller fin).
sources.rollRateMaxRadS: TUNING KNOB — ~51.6 deg/s, brisk mid-jet roll (lighter and shorter-span than the 737, so quicker than its 15 deg/s but well below the F-5E's fighter roll).
sources.damping/stiffness: TUNING KNOBS — rollDampingPerS 3.0 with the roll rate above gives a crisp but not twitchy bizjet roll feel; pitch omega_n = sqrt(3.0) = 1.73 rad/s, zeta = 2.5/(2*1.73) = 0.72 (well damped).
sources.refDynamicPressurePa: TUNING KNOB — 6500 Pa, above the b738's 6000 Pa: a lighter, smaller-wing jet reaches this qBar at a comparable speed, so control authority saturates through the same normal speed band.
sources.trimAlphaCenterRad: TUNING KNOB — 1.7 deg, near the cruise AoA so trim near centre is roughly hands-off cruise.
sources.trimAlphaRangeRad: TUNING KNOB — +-7.4 deg trim authority, enough to trim from approach AoA to cruise AoA.
sources.propulsion: TUNING KNOBS — 2x flat-rated turbofan via the shared T=eta*P/max(V,peak): propPeakSpeedMs 250 m/s sits above cruise TAS at FL430 (~227 m/s) so thrust there is constant with speed (flat-rated), reduced only by the density lapse above this class's turbofanCornerM. maxPowerW 6.5 MW gives eta*P/250 = 0.85*6.5e6/250 = 22.1 kN full-throttle rated thrust; T/W ~0.20 at 11.5 t — below a real Citation Latitude's static T/W (2x PW306D1 ~5,907 lbf static each, source verification pending), which is honest for a cruise-oriented flat-rated model. maxPowerW is pinned with cd0 and turbofanCornerM by the FL430 cruise-Mach + SL-climb + 45,000 ft-ceiling triple. afterburnerFactor 1.0 (no afterburner, unlike the F-5E). lapseModel "turbofan" (shared with b738/f5e).
sources.turbofanCornerM: TUNING KNOB — 6400 m (FL210). The turbofan flat-rating corner is now per-class DATA (forces.ts turbofanPowerLapse defaults to the shared TURBOFAN_CORNER_M = 11582 m / FL380 when omitted; b738/f5e omit it and are unchanged). Biz cruises at FL430, above the shared FL380 corner, where an FL380 corner fixes the SL-full / cruise-85% thrust ratio at ~1.5x regardless of drag — which capped realistic-cd0 SL climb at ~650-900 fpm (see task-1-report.md derivation). Lowering biz's corner to FL210 puts more of the cruise climb in the lapsed regime, so holding FL430 cruise Mach demands more rated thrust, and that thrust — unlapsed at sea level — restores a realistic SL climb margin at an honest cd0 (0.023). Pinned by the FL430-cruise + SL-climb + 45,000 ft-ceiling triple; not a published figure (source verification pending).
sources.propEfficiency: 0.85 — the eta in T = eta*P/max(V,peak), matching b738/f5e; not a real prop efficiency (the aircraft has no propeller). Kept near 1 so maxPowerW carries the tuning.
sources.lapseModel: "turbofan" — selects forces.ts turbofanPowerLapse (flat-rated to TURBOFAN_CORNER_M, then density falloff). Shared with b738/f5e, chosen by this key not a class branch (decisions AF-002).
sources.afterburnerFactor: 1.0 — turbofan, no afterburner (Citation-class bizjets have none).
sources.limits.vneIasMs: Vmo ~305 KIAS = 156.9 m/s. Source verification pending.
sources.limits.vnoIasMs: ~288 KIAS = 148.0 m/s, a display caution reference below Vmo. Source verification pending.
sources.limits.vfeIasMs: ~204 KIAS = 105.0 m/s flap placard (most-restrictive detent); display only. Source verification pending.
sources.mmo: 0.80 — typical Citation-class Mmo. Source verification pending.
sources.vleIasMs: ~220 KIAS = 113.0 m/s Vle/Vlo placard. Source verification pending.
sources.gLimits: +3.0 / -1.0, bizjet clean flight-envelope limits (between the 737's +2.5 and a fighter's higher clamp). Pinned by the g-clamp envelope test (reached from a 320 kt entry at FL200).
sources.serviceCeilingM: 13,716 m (45,000 ft) — a real Citation Latitude certified service ceiling, now honest in-model: at biz's plausible cd0 (0.023) + maxPowerW (6.5 MW) + turbofanCornerM (FL210), full-throttle best climb at 45,000 ft measures ~258 fpm — a real ceiling (inside the test's 0-500 fpm band), reached because the per-class FL210 corner lapses stratospheric thrust enough to run the climb out at the certified altitude rather than thousands of feet above it.
sources.flaps: 0/1/2/FULL — simplified bizjet schedule; dCL0/dStallAlpha/dCD0 are TUNING KNOBS giving monotonically falling stall speeds and rising drag across the schedule.
sources.display: ASI 60-400 kt spans the jet band, matching b738; attitudeStyle ball (EFIS horizon disc).
sources.gear: retractable — Citation-class bizjets have retractable gear.
sources.lookArc: // tunable — mapped to the AIRLINER family, not GA/turboprop (issue #44 follow-up, owner's four families didn't name a bizjet): a Citation-class flight deck is a swept transport-style cockpit like the 737's, just smaller, not a bubble canopy or a strut-and-doorframe GA cabin. Same numbers as b738 until an owner live-feel pass says otherwise.
